sec: Anatomy and embryology of pituitary gland

items.q: The pituitary gland is historically designated in endocrine physiology as the:
items.exp: The pituitary gland is designated as the master gland of endocrine. (Book p936)

items.q: The anterior pituitary gland arises embryologically as an upgrowth from the roof of the ___.
items.exp: The anterior pituitary originates as an upgrowth from the roof of the oral ectoderm forming Rathke's pouch. (Book p936)

items.q: Match the pituitary lobe to its embryological origin — 1) Anterior pituitary 2) Posterior pituitary … A) Upgrowth from roof of oral ectoderm (Rathke's pouch) B) Downgrowth from floor of third ventricle (Neurohypophysis)
items.exp: The anterior pituitary arises from oral ectoderm (Rathke's pouch) while the posterior pituitary develops as a downgrowth from the floor of the third ventricle. (Book p936)

items.q: The most common etiology of congenital hypopituitarism is:
items.exp: The most common cause of congenital hypopituitarism is pituitary dysplasia. (Book p936)

items.q: Assess the statements on congenital hypopituitarism: I Only the anterior pituitary is typically involved in pituitary dysplasia. II Posterior pituitary function is routinely lost.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: In congenital hypopituitarism secondary to pituitary dysplasia, only the anterior pituitary is involved. (Book p936)

items.q: Which transcription factor mutation represents the most important molecular defect in congenital hypopituitarism?
items.exp: Prop-1 mutation is the most important transcription factor defect underlying congenital hypopituitarism. (Book p936)

items.q: A newborn infant presents with a solitary central maxillary incisor and midline facial cleft. Defective midline migration of cells during development from which embryological site explains this presentation?
items.exp: Rathke's pouch cells migrate from the nasopharynx to the brain; defects in midline migration lead to craniofacial anomalies like single central incisors, bifid uvula, and cleft lip. (Book p936)

items.q: Identify the anomaly that is NOT part of the midline craniofacial defects linked with Rathke's pouch migratory failure:
items.exp: Midline craniofacial defects resulting from abnormal migration of Rathke's pouch cells include single central incisors, bifid uvula, and cleft lip, but not mandibular prognathism. (Book p936)

items.q: What is the normal baseline weight of the adult human pituitary gland?
items.exp: The pituitary gland normally weighs 600 mg. (Book p936)

items.q: During normal pregnancy, the human pituitary gland undergoes physiological hyperplasia and enlarges to a weight of ___.
items.exp: During pregnancy the pituitary gland enlarges from 600 mg to 1 gm. (Book p936)

items.q: A 28-year-old woman suffers massive postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) during delivery. Compromised blood supply to her hypertrophied gland leads to ischemic necrosis, termed:
items.exp: Severe blood loss from postpartum hemorrhage compromises blood supply to the enlarged gestational pituitary, resulting in Sheehan syndrome. (Book p936)

items.q: Match the physiological state of the pituitary gland to its corresponding weight — 1) Baseline non-pregnant weight 2) Enlarged weight in pregnancy … A) 600 mg B) 1 gm
items.exp: The pituitary gland weighs 600 mg at baseline and increases to 1 gm during pregnancy. (Book p936)
